docs.title: Adding Images
docs.text: Images can be added to any page. There are two steps: uploading the image file to your repo and referencing it in your markdown.

docs.title: Step 1 — Upload your image
docs.text:
We recommend keeping all images in docs/assets/images/ to stay organized.

On GitHub.com (no terminal) 1. Navigate to `docs/assets/` in your repo 2. Click **Add file → Upload files** 3. Drag and drop your image or click to browse 4. Click **Commit changes** > If the `images/` subfolder doesn't exist yet, you can create it by naming your file `images/my-image.png` in the file name field — GitHub will create the folder automatically. Locally (terminal) 
# from the root of your repo
cp ~/Downloads/my-image.png docs/assets/images/my-image.png
git add .
git commit -m "Add image"
git push

docs.title: Step 2 — Add the image to your page
docs.text:
Open the .md file where you want the image to appear and use this syntax:

![A description of the image](../assets/images/my-image.png)

The text in square brackets is the alt text — a short description of the image. It is important for accessibility and should always be filled in.

docs.title: Getting the path right
docs.text:
The path to your image is relative to the markdown file you are editing. Use the table below:

Your markdown file Path to use docs/index.md assets/images/my-image.png docs/how-to/page.md ../assets/images/my-image.png docs/how-to/sub/page.md ../../assets/images/my-image.png

Each ../ moves up one folder level toward docs/.

docs.title: Controlling image size
docs.text:
Add a width attribute after the path:

![My image](../assets/images/my-image.png){ width="400" }

Or as a percentage of the page width:

![My image](../assets/images/my-image.png){ width="60%" }

docs.title: Adding a caption
docs.text:
<figure markdown>
  ![A bar chart showing gene expression levels](../assets/images/my-image.png)
  <figcaption>Figure 1. Gene expression levels across conditions.</figcaption>
</figure>

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Supported formats: PNG, JPG, GIF, SVG, WebP
  • PNG is recommended for screenshots and diagrams
  • Avoid spaces in file names — use hyphens or underscores: my-figure.png ✅ my figure.png ❌
  • Keep images reasonably sized before uploading — large images slow down page load

docs.title: Site Structure & Navigation
docs.text: Your MkDocs site is controlled by two things: the files in your docs/ folder and the mkdocs.yml file at the root of your repo. This page explains how they work together.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Every page on your site is a markdown file (.md) inside the docs/ folder. The mkdocs.yml file tells MkDocs what to call each page and how to organize them in the navigation menu.

your-repo/
├── mkdocs.yml        ← controls site settings and navigation
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md      ← your home page (required)
│   ├── about.md
│   └── 01_section/
│       └── page.md

docs.title: The nav section in mkdocs.yml
docs.text:
The nav: block in mkdocs.yml defines your site's menu. Each entry is a label and a path to a file in docs/.

# mkdocs.yml — located at the root of your repo

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - About: about.md
  - My Section:
    - First Page: 01_section/first-page.md
    - Second Page: 01_section/second-page.md

The label on the left (e.g. Home, About) is what appears in the menu. The path on the right is relative to the docs/ folder.

docs.title: Adding a new page
docs.text:
Step 1 — Create the file

On GitHub.com (no terminal) 1. Navigate to your `docs/` folder on GitHub.com 2. Click **Add file → Create new file** 3. Name your file, e.g. `my-new-page.md` or `01_section/my-new-page.md` 4. Add some content and click **Commit changes** Locally (terminal) 
# from the root of your repo
touch docs/my-new-page.md

Step 2 — Add it to the nav

Open mkdocs.yml and add a line under nav::

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - My New Page: my-new-page.md  # ← add this

docs.title: Adding a new section
docs.text:
To group pages under a section heading in the menu, indent them under a label with no file path:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - My Section:             # ← section label, no file path
    - Page One: 01_section/page-one.md
    - Page Two: 01_section/page-two.md

It helps to organize your files into matching folders inside docs/, but it is not required — the folder structure and the nav are independent.

docs.title: Changing the site name and description
docs.text:
At the top of mkdocs.yml:

# mkdocs.yml — located at the root of your repo

site_name: My Project Documentation   # ← appears in the browser tab and header
site_description: A short description # ← used for search and SEO

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• The file docs/index.md is your home page and is required
  • File and folder names cannot contain spaces — use hyphens or underscores
  • The order of items in nav: controls the order they appear in the menu
  • After editing mkdocs.yml on GitHub.com, your site will redeploy automatically in ~2 minutes

docs.title: Embedding Video
docs.text: The recommended way to add video to your site is to embed from YouTube or Vimeo. This keeps your repo small and fast — the video file itself lives on the external platform.

docs.title: Embedding a YouTube video
docs.text:
Step 1 — Get the embed code from YouTube

  1. Go to the YouTube video you want to embed
  2. Click Share below the video
  3. Click Embed
  4. Copy the <iframe> code

It will look something like this:

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>

Step 2 — Paste it into your markdown file

MkDocs supports raw HTML in markdown files, so you can paste the iframe directly:

## My Video Title

Some introductory text here.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allowfullscreen></iframe>

Replace VIDEO_ID with the actual ID from your video's URL, e.g. for https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ the ID is dQw4w9WgXcQ.

docs.title: Making the video responsive
docs.text:
The default iframe has a fixed width and may not look great on smaller screens. Wrap it in a div to make it scale with the page:

<div style="position: relative; padding-bottom: 56.25%; height: 0; overflow: hidden;">
  <iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
    style="position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%;"
    frameborder="0"
    allowfullscreen>
  </iframe>
</div>

56.25% maintains a standard 16:9 aspect ratio.

docs.title: Embedding a Vimeo video
docs.text: The process is the same — go to the video on Vimeo, click Share, copy the embed code, and paste it into your markdown file.

docs.title: Linking to an externally hosted video file
docs.text:
If your video is hosted on a shared drive or institutional storage and you have a direct link, you can add it as a standard hyperlink:

[Watch the demo video](https://your-institution.edu/path/to/video.mp4)

Or if the hosting platform supports it, you can use an HTML video player:

<video width="560" controls>
  <source src="https://your-institution.edu/path/to/video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Never commit large video files directly to your repo
  • YouTube and Vimeo are the most reliable embedding options
  • Make sure your YouTube video is set to public or unlisted — private videos will not embed
